headline: Highest risk is medium: Botpress can ingest content while ComfyUI exposes file-backed model/workflow surfaces, creating plausible injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict paths, but no direct shared-channel evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or input provenance controls, while ComfyUI exposes file-backed workflow/model surfaces and an asynchronous queue. A plausible pathway exists if Botpress consumes ComfyUI-generated text or files as trusted instructions. The pairwise interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Botpress ingests ComfyUI output as instructions or prompts
IF a shared filesystem or copied artifact bridges the two agents
mitigations: Disable any automatic parsing of ComfyUI outputs by Botpress
Use a manual review step before Botpress consumes generated text
Separate working directories for the two agents
Prefix all ComfyUI outputs with non-executable metadata headers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has network egress set to none, but ComfyUI can access model files and workflows on disk, and both profiles expose file-related surfaces. If they share a workspace, Botpress could surface content from files that ComfyUI reads or writes, creating a sensitive-data path. The evidence is indirect and no secrets are declared, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or workspace
IF sensitive prompts, workflows, or model metadata are stored in that shared location
mitigations: Keep separate directories and mounts for each agent
Store sensitive artifacts outside any shared workspace
Review Botpress logs for file-content echoes
Restrict ComfyUI model/workflow folders to read-only where possible
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while ComfyUI cannot modify git state, write the filesystem, or spawn subprocesses according to its profile. That limits direct write-write conflict. A conflict still exists if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or package environment, but that requires unusual setup and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same workspace or dependency environment
IF package installation by Botpress targets files used by ComfyUI
mitigations: Pin Botpress package installs to an isolated environment
Avoid sharing a git checkout between agents
Run ComfyUI from a read-only deployment directory
Check for concurrent writes before maintenance actions
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a support-oriented agent that may generate user-facing content, and ComfyUI can consume workflows and outputs asynchronously. If Botpress-produced text or metadata is fed into ComfyUI without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect image-generation workflows or misleading artifacts. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress output is used as ComfyUI workflow input without validation
IF ComfyUI actions are triggered from Botpress-generated metadata
mitigations: Insert a validation step before ComfyUI consumes Botpress output
Require human approval for workflow changes
Log and diff workflow inputs before execution
Use schema checks on any exchanged JSON
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and no regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented in the profiles. Botpress has no declared secrets handling and ComfyUI is offline-capable, so there is no clear compliance mismatch. The other agent is cited because the assessment is pairwise, but the evidence does not show a residency or certification conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent
IF deployment policy requires a specific residency or retention guarantee not documented here
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Document retention and residency expectations
Review deployment logs for unexpected data classes
Keep both agents on the same compliance boundary
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit controls
